original_images_role: Exact originals retained in publication/reference; these PNG/SVG exports are distinct numerical equivalents.

figures.caption: Fixed FULL global and classical identities. Open points are the five paired optimizer seeds; diamonds and whiskers show mean ± sample seed SD, not confidence intervals. Metrics average clients equally. Global and personal checkpoints were selected separately on VAL.

Fixed FULL personal neural identities. Open points are the five paired optimizer seeds; diamonds and whiskers show mean ± sample seed SD, not confidence intervals. Metrics average clients equally. Global and personal checkpoints were selected separately on VAL.

Observed versus forecast regional monthly rainfall, 2017–2024. Each panel shows all 480 CAAA global FULL seed-specific forecasts (96 dates × five seeds), and the 96 distinct TRAIN monthly climatology forecasts. Dashed line: 1:1; dotted vertical line: local gradient-TRAIN q80. Panels have separate scales. Negative forecasts are retained. Repeated seeds add forecasts, not independent observations.

Fixed original, enriched and uniform TRAIN input affinities on a shared 0–1 scale. TRAIN targets run 1983-01 through 2007-11 (299 per client). These structural summaries use privileged aligned TRAIN anomalies/descriptors; they are neither causal effects nor forecast skill. Row-normalized trainer weights remain in the source CSV.

Seed-42 development grids on January 2011–November 2016 VAL. (a) Shared learning rate. (b) Six method-specific proximal μ grids. (c) Fifteen quarter-step simplex triples plus the (0.3,0.3,0.4) anchor; color uses its own validation scale. Rings mark selected candidates. (d) All sixty saved validation rounds for the selected LR, CAAA μ and coefficient candidates. Validation was reused for tuning/checkpoint selection; these are developmental scores, not independent accuracy estimates.

Fixed (0.3,0.3,0.4) anchor minus each separate removal. Points and lines are saved paired differences and marginal unadjusted 95% circular block12 intervals. Positive R²/negative RMSE favors the anchor. The selected (1,0,0) primary is a distinct identity. Intervals are not simultaneous; block6/24 sensitivities remain in companion evidence.

Separate client precision–recall curves for the three FULL global identities at fixed illustrative seed 42. Scores are predicted heavy-event probabilities. Events exceed the local gradient-TRAIN q80; dash-dot line is observed evaluation prevalence. No pooled-client curve is shown. This realization is not an event-scale flood-warning validation.

Per-client heavy-event recall, average precision and rainfall tail RMSE for fixed FULL global/personal identities. Small points: five seeds; diamonds and whiskers: mean ± sample seed SD, not confidence intervals. Recall uses probability ≥0.5; AP uses continuous probabilities; tail RMSE scores observed months exceeding local TRAIN q80. Proportion whiskers stop at 0/100% with arrows when SD extends beyond those bounds. Seed values themselves remain in [0,100%]; repeated seeds do not add observed events.

Information-sharing study, fixed tick60. Points show mean macro RMSE; ranges are optimizer-seed minimum–maximum, not confidence intervals. Own/shared denotes local/shared TRAIN input scaling. K1/K5/K20 is synchronization cadence in local ticks. Required numeric payload sums recipients and includes federated initial/final model delivery; central pooled payload includes engineered examples/final delivery. Transport and research audit traffic are excluded. Dashed line is TRAIN climatology. No network-latency or compute saving is implied.

Common VAL checkpoint sensitivity for the same fitted policies. Primary fixed tick60 and secondary common selection among ticks20/40/60 are shown for global/local paths. Personal diagnostic paths remain separately identified in model_summary_ALL_endpoints.csv. Checkpoint communication is separately priced; optimizer repeats and endpoint forecasts do not add independent observations.
